writeup: TIC 468010975 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 10.1260 days. The primary eclipse produces a 6.30% dimming in the star's brightness, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 112.1 using automated analysis of TESS photometry. A secondary eclipse was also detected at 9.7 sigma significance, occurring at orbital phase -0.39. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 30.1, though the centroid offset of 1.7 arcsec warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.44 suggests moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing system rather than a false positive.
